newsitem.title: USA: Medaphis slips as takeover rumors quiet.
newsitem.headline: Medaphis slips as takeover rumors quiet.

text.p: Medaphis Corp shares dropped Thursday after the company's plans to divest certain business units quieted rumors that the Atlanta-based firm would be an imminent takeover candidate, analysts said.
Medaphis dipped 1-3/4 to 11-1/4 amid news that the company may divest its Healthcare Recoveries Inc and is assessing alternatives for its BSG Corp unit.
Medaphis' stock has rallied recently among market rumors that the billing, accounts receivable and management services company would be an attractive acquisition target.
Medaphis Chairman David McDowell said in a prepared statement Wednesday "1997 will be a year of transition."
Analysts said suitors may wait until Medaphis reorganizes its units, improves its balance sheet and refocuses before proceeding with a takeover.

"The problem is if you buy the whole thing, you buy the physician billing system, which is under pressure. If you buy the whole thing, you buy the problem," said Marie Rossi, an analyst with Dean Witter Reynolds.
Analyst said Medaphis would be more attractive in parts -- rather than as a whole.
"I can't imagine who would want to buy the whole thing given the highly disparate nature of the units," said Andrew May, an analyst with J.C. Bradford.

Analysts also said Medaphis has suffered recently from a distracted management team, class action lawsuits, weakness in the Medaphis Physician Services Corp unit and the reorganization of the Imonics unit.

After the market closed Wednesday, Medaphis posted a fourth quarter loss of $103.7 million or $1.45 a share on revenues of $142.9 million. The quarter included $138.9 million in restructuring and other charges related to its decision to abandon its reengineering program and to shut down the Imonics unit.
In the prior year's fourth quarter, the company posted a net loss of $1.15 million or $0.02 a share on revenues of $144.7 million.
